body: Implementation is the test. The agreement is the current legal and diplomatic frame of climate politics, not a solved problem. Editorial draft for this timeline, not a substitute for specialist literature.
sources: UNFCCC, Paris Agreement; Falkner, The Paris Agreement and the new logic of international climate politics

title: COVID-19 pandemic
summary: A novel coronavirus spreads worldwide, killing millions and shutting down much of ordinary public life.
body: mRNA vaccines arrived at unprecedented speed. The political, educational, and economic aftershocks are still being counted. Editorial draft for this timeline, not a substitute for specialist literature.
sources: WHO, COVID-19 Dashboard; Tooze, Shutdown

title: Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine
summary: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, returning high-intensity war to Europe.
body: The 2014 seizure of Crimea was the prelude. Energy, refugees, NATO, and nuclear risk all re-entered European politics at once. Editorial draft for this timeline, not a substitute for specialist literature.
sources: Plokhy, The Russo-Ukrainian War; Snyder, lectures and essays on the invasion

title: Western Roman Empire
summary: Duration of the Roman imperial order in the west, from Augustus to 476.
body: A long imperial structure, not a single event. Rendered as a context bar so neighbouring histories can be seen against it. Editorial draft for this timeline, not a substitute for specialist literature.
sources: Garnsey and Saller, The Roman Empire

title: Han dynasty
summary: The Han empire sets much of the institutional pattern later called imperial China.
body: Western then Eastern Han, with a Xin interregnum. Civil service, Confucian canon, and expansion into Inner Asia all belong here. Editorial draft for this timeline, not a substitute for specialist literature.
sources: Lewis, The Early Chinese Empires

title: Byzantine Empire
summary: The Roman empire continues from Constantinople until the Ottoman conquest.
body: Its inhabitants called themselves Romans. The span is the eastern imperial context behind medieval Balkan, Anatolian, and Black Sea history. Editorial draft for this timeline, not a substitute for specialist literature.
sources: Herrin, Byzantium

title: Abbasid Caliphate
summary: Abbasid rule, at first imperial and later often symbolic, from the overthrow of the Umayyads to the Mongol sack of Baghdad.
body: Real power fragmented early. The cultural prestige of the caliphate outlasted its armies. Editorial draft for this timeline, not a substitute for specialist literature.
sources: Kennedy, When Baghdad Ruled the Muslim World

title: Ottoman Empire
summary: Ottoman imperial span from the traditional founding under Osman to the end of the sultanate.
body: A multi-ethnic empire at the junction of Europe and the Middle East. Tanzimat, world war, and nationalism ended it. Editorial draft for this timeline, not a substitute for specialist literature.
sources: Finkel, Osman’s Dream

title: Ming dynasty
summary: Ming imperial span from the expulsion of the Yuan to the Qing conquest of Beijing.
body: Great walls, a commercial economy, and a late crisis of climate, silver, and rebellion. Context bar for early modern East Asia. Editorial draft for this timeline, not a substitute for specialist literature.
sources: Brook, The Troubled Empire

title: Qing dynasty
summary: Manchu-led imperial span over China and Inner Asia until the 1911 Revolution.
body: High Qing expansion, then the long 19th-century crisis. Context for opium wars, Taiping, and reform. Editorial draft for this timeline, not a substitute for specialist literature.
sources: Rowe, China’s Last Empire

title: Mughal Empire
summary: Timurid-Mughal rule in South Asia from Babur’s victory at Panipat to the aftermath of 1857.
body: Akbar’s settlement, later Aurangzeb, and a long twilight under Company power. A context bar for early modern India. Editorial draft for this timeline, not a substitute for specialist literature.
sources: Richards, The Mughal Empire

title: Tokugawa shogunate
summary: Tokugawa bakufu from Ieyasu’s appointment as shogun to the Meiji Restoration.
body: Peace, status hierarchy, and controlled foreign contact. Context for the shock of Perry and the Meiji break. Editorial draft for this timeline, not a substitute for specialist literature.
sources: Totman, Early Modern Japan

title: Spanish overseas empire
summary: Span of the major Spanish overseas empire from Columbus to the loss of Cuba and the Philippines.
body: American silver, Catholic mission, and a global monarchy. Independence in the 1820s ended most of it; 1898 finished the remnant. Editorial draft for this timeline, not a substitute for specialist literature.
sources: Elliott, Empires of the Atlantic World

title: British Empire (union to late decolonization)
summary: A long context bar from the Union of 1707 to the handover of Hong Kong.
body: The empire was not one thing for 290 years. The bar exists so other events can be seen against British imperial time. Editorial draft for this timeline, not a substitute for specialist literature.
sources: Darwin, The Empire Project

title: Soviet Union
summary: Union of Soviet Socialist Republics from formal creation to dissolution.
body: Stalinism, victory in 1945, and a superpower that lost an economic and legitimacy contest. Context bar for the short 20th century. Editorial draft for this timeline, not a substitute for specialist literature.
sources: Suny, The Soviet Experiment
